sketches.title: Right of Way
sketches.premise: You and your opponent build a traffic scene one vehicle or road user at a time. On your turn, your entrant must legally and physically take priority over the thing currently at the front; the judge checks whether the new arrival genuinely controls the next movement, not merely survives it.
sketches.criterion: A move beats what stands by making its path, signal, authority, or position force the standing road user to yield or stop; dodging, waiting it out, being harder to hit, and using a larger copy of the same road user do not count.
sketches.move_shape: Name one road user and the traffic rule or action that makes the current one yield: “I am a police car, lights flashing; the truck pulls over.”
sketches.first_card: A stalled bicycle blocking the lane.

sketches.title: Red Means Stop
sketches.premise: The road is moving, and every turn adds one traffic signal, sign, barrier, or official instruction. Your new control must directly cancel the instruction currently ruling the road, turning a live command into a different lawful order; the first failed override loses.
sketches.criterion: A move beats the standing control only by clearly changing, invalidating, or superseding its command with a mechanism such as a new signal, officer, or emergency rule; ignoring it, slipping around it, or making the same command stronger is a loss.
sketches.move_shape: Name a traffic control and state the exact command that replaces the current one: “I am a green light for the cross street; the red light no longer governs this lane.”
sketches.first_card: A green light telling traffic to go.

sketches.title: Road Hazard
sketches.premise: One player places a hazard on the roadway; the other must answer with a single road thing that removes, contains, or makes that hazard harmless. Then the roles switch, so every answer becomes the next danger. No one wins by merely swerving around trouble: the road must be made safe.
sketches.criterion: The response beats the standing hazard by physically removing it, sealing it, repairing it, or stopping its harmful effect; avoiding it, enduring it, or offering a bigger version of the same hazard fails.
sketches.move_shape: Name one road thing and say how it neutralizes the hazard: “I am a tow truck; I drag the wreck off the lane.”
sketches.first_card: A deep pothole in the road.

sketches.title: Lane Change
sketches.premise: You are competing to control a moving lane. Each turn names a vehicle or road feature that forces the thing ahead to change lanes, merge, or surrender its lane through a clear traffic interaction; the scene keeps shifting until one demand cannot be made.
sketches.criterion: A move beats the standing thing by directly forcing its lane position to change through size, signal, law, blockage, or maneuver; merely passing beside it, staying in another lane, or using a bigger cousin of it does not count.
sketches.move_shape: Name the new lane-changing force and its action: “I am a bus pulling into the lane; the car must merge left.”
sketches.first_card: A car cruising alone in the right lane.

sketches.title: Traffic Jam
sketches.premise: Players alternate adding one standing road presence to a growing jam. Your addition must directly cause the current front presence to stop, compress, or lose movement, while the opponent then tries to break that jam with something that restores motion. The judge tracks the immediate road effect, not dramatic size.
sketches.criterion: A move beats what stands by directly stopping or restoring its movement through a concrete road mechanism; merely being stuck too, waiting longer, or adding a larger version of the same obstruction is a loss.
sketches.move_shape: Name one road presence and explain its immediate effect: “I am a road crew closing the lane; the taxi must stop.”
sketches.first_card: A taxi stopped at a crowded intersection.

sketches.title: Signal Noise
sketches.premise: Each turn is one clear message sent by a road user: a horn, hand signal, indicator, sign, or shouted warning. Your message must directly defeat the message currently standing by making it false, unreadable, or officially overridden; the judge ignores poetic volume and checks the communication mechanism.
sketches.criterion: A signal beats the standing signal by clearly contradicting, blocking, scrambling, or officially replacing its meaning; ignoring it, shouting louder, or using a related signal from the same family without a real mechanism fails.
sketches.move_shape: Name a sender, its signal, and how it defeats the current meaning: “I am a police officer waving traffic through; my hand signal overrides the turn arrow.”
